claims.statement: ParamBinding (services/ParamBinding.h, port of useParameter.ts) is a view's handle on one host parameter, values normalised 0..1. It brackets drag writes in beginGesture/dragTo/endGesture so the host records one automation gesture, and inbound parameter echoes are ignored while the pointer is down (a stale echo must not snap the live value back). Change notifications fire on the message thread; an unknown id (a build without that parameter) yields an inert binding that reads 0 and swallows writes, so views never null-check.

MidiMapper (plugin/include/MidiMapper.h) handles MIDI CC/note → target mapping with Learn, and lives in the processor (not the device layer) so the same map/learn/settings work identically in standalone and in DAW hosts; it serializes with plugin state via getStateInformation. Targets are four kinds: APVTS parameters, positional block powers (block1Power/rightBlock1Power — positional addressing is deliberate because block ids are ephemeral), stereo mode, and presetPrevious/presetNext steps. Behavior derivation: CC on a continuous parameter is absolute; CC on a toggle/trigger target fires once per press (value >= 64 fires, and a < 64 value also fires unless it follows a >= 64 from the same control — momentary release); note-on toggles continuous targets; program change n loads the nth preset in list order.

A block param field round-trips only if it exists in all FOUR state places: (1) getChainState in plugin/src/ProcessorChain.cpp (the BlockRow struct, the copyLane copy, AND params->setProperty('<field>',…) in serializeChain); (2) parseItem in plugin/ui/model/ChainState.cpp (item.<field> = num(v["params"], "<field>", default)); (3) updateBlockParam in plugin/src/ProcessorChain.cpp (the param == "<field>" branch); (4) ProcessorState.cpp (blockState.setProperty + getProperty restore). Missing any one = 'works sonically, snaps back to default on sync'. Two families sit in these four places: (a) CHAIN-LAYER dry-gain params — convDry, and reverbDry since the 2026-10-13 R1 pass — whose updateBlockParam branch does NOT call an engine setParams (the gain is applied in the chain's mix loop on the dry term only); (b) ENGINE params like reverbSharedMod (R2 shared Mod depth, 0..1 clamped), reverbWave (R2 Digital Shape, int 0..kNumWaves-1 clamped), and reverbLoCut (T-DAT-001, 0..1 clamped, stored fraction) — whose updateBlockParam branch stores the clamped value AND calls block->reverb.setParams(block->reverbParams()).

The node-view (grid block interface) toggle is persisted as a UiPrefs key, not a block/chain param: UiPrefs::kNodeView = "t3k.nodeView" (UiPrefs.h:68), a plain getBool/setBool preference (default false = gallery view). The gallery|node toggle in PluginHeader (NodeViewToggle, a StereoModeToggle-style 80x36 two-segment control) reads it at construction via services_.prefs.getBool(UiPrefs::kNodeView, false) (PluginHeader.cpp:47) and fires onNodeViewToggle(nodeView) on click; PluginRoot writes the pref back with prefs.setBool and calls chainScreen().setView(nodeView) to swap the visible view.

The gallery/node view toggle is persisted as UiPrefs::kNodeView = "t3k.nodeView" (plugin/ui/services/UiPrefs.h:68); ChainScreen reads it at startup (getBool default false) and calls setView() to activate the node view, and the PluginHeader toggle writes it back on every click.

removeChainBlock is IN-PLACE (node-view batch 2 law, reaffirmed in the m06828 batch, commit 72f48ea): after pushing history it erases the block and inserts a FRESH ChainBlock of type INSERT at the erased position, so a mid-lane removal leaves lane size unchanged with the gap in place (no left-shift of neighbours); a subsequent addEffectBlock/landToneBlock into that index fills the gap in place. Inserts themselves are not removable (the insert branch returns false). Covered by AddAtSlot.MidLaneGapIsFilledInPlace / TrailingInsertIsFilledAtTheEnd (test/src/add_at_slot_tests.cpp — re-baselined to the floor-only 6-slot tail by 72f48ea) and the new m06828 DspTests ProcessorTest.RemoveLeavesInsertGapWithoutLeftShift + ProcessorTest.RemoveRejectsInsertBlocks (test/src/processor_tests.cpp).

ChainScreen::setView(false) sweeps the PluginRoot overlay layer with Popover::dismissAll: a strip mode/type menu is a Popover parented to the overlay, and hiding the strip only removes the ANCESTOR — the panel would ghost over the gallery (ComponentMovementWatcher fires only on the anchor's own visible-flag toggle, never on an ancestor's).

convRawSeconds is the raw, untrimmed IR length in seconds — the cap the Start/End UI faces use (scales::convTrimScale, KnobScale.h:675, so a window can never point past a short IR's tail). It is engine-observed, not dialable: set in getChainState (BlockRow.convRawSeconds at ProcessorChain.cpp:1327, filled from block->conv.rawSeconds() when an IR is loaded at :1452, serialized only if > 0 at :1638-1639), parseItem (num(v, "convRawSeconds", 0.0) — ChainState.cpp:251, ChainState.h:219), and ProcessorState.cpp (setProperty at :315, guarded by block.conv.hasIr()) — three of the four state places. There is deliberately NO updateBlockParam branch (nothing user-written may touch it). A missing key falls back to 0.0, and convTrimScale turns that into a 1 s face rather than a 0-cap knob. The on-load defaults (m04426/m04437, commit 9a5c3c8) reset convStartS=0.0 / convEndS=rawSeconds() / convPitch=0.5 in loadConvIr (ProcessorChain.cpp:463-467) before setParams, so switching to a shorter IR never leaves a stale trim window.

T-DAT-001 engine param reverbLoCut (0..1 clamped, default 0 = bit-pass) and the conv trim fields convStartS/convEndS (seconds, clamped to 0..kMaxIrSeconds=30) both follow the four-state-place rule. Line numbers as of commit 9c203cb: reverbLoCut: (1) ChainBlock.h:412 field + reverbParams() at :426 ending reverbSharedMod, reverbWave, reverbLoCut (aggregate end :436) + ProcessorChain.cpp BlockRow :1312, row mirror :1431, serializeChain :1611; (2) ChainState.h:187, ChainState.cpp parseItem :230; (3) ProcessorChain.cpp isEffectParam :2082 + updateBlockParam :2381-2382 (jlimit 0..1 + block->reverb.setParams); (4) ProcessorState.cpp :289 / restore :483. convStartS/convEndS: (1) ChainBlock.h:458-459, BlockRow :1319, mirror :1438-1439, serializeChain :1618-1619; (2) ChainState.h:202-203, ChainState.cpp :238-239; (3) isEffectParam :2082, updateBlockParam :2400-2406 (jlimit 0..ConvolutionReverb::kMaxIrSeconds); (4) ProcessorState.cpp :296-297 / restore :505-506. Their per-IR UI faces come from scales::convTrimScale(rawSeconds) (KnobScale.h:675), not a toStored split — the stored values are always absolute seconds.

The compressor TYPE axis: compType (int; per-mode sub-model; 0 = the mode's own engine, the only type today — Compressor::numTypes(mode) returns 1 for every mode). Four places (line numbers as of commit 9c203cb): (1) ChainBlock.h:365 field int compType = 0 (immediately after compMode :364) + ProcessorChain.cpp BlockRow :1298, copyLane mirror :1400, serializeChain :1575; (2) ChainState.h:160 + ChainState.cpp parseItem :190; (3) ProcessorChain.cpp isEffectParam :2082 + updateBlockParam :2274-2275 (stores verbatim via static_cast<int> — no clamp here, the engine clamps via setParams jlimit 0..numTypes-1) + appends to compressor setParams at :2279; (4) ProcessorState.cpp :238 / restore :393 (cast to int, verbatim). compType is the 11th and last field of Compressor::Params, so every block->compressor.setParams({...}) call site passes block->compType last.

KnobScale (plugin/ui/core/KnobScale.h, port of knobScale.ts) keeps three domains separate: normalised 0..1 knob position, a DISPLAY unit for the drag readout and type-in, and a STORAGE contract via toStored/fromStored. knobToStored()/knobFromStored() fall back to toDisplay/fromDisplay when no explicit storage pair is declared. Knobs whose stored domain is 0..1 but whose display unit is human MUST declare toStored/fromStored or the tile writes the display unit into a 0..1 param, the engine clamps to 1.0, and the next resync snaps the knob back to max (the 2026-10-06 Heads glitch). Current toStored list (line numbers as of commit 9c203cb): delayHeads (1..4 heads), compClip (0..2 raw depth behind a 0..200% face), convGain ±24 dB (KnobScale.h:613), convDwell ±18 dB (KnobScale.h:634 — a ±18 dB display window over the SHARED 0..1 input-gain store with identity toStored, same store as convGain; 0.25..0.75 of the dial spans the ±18 dB window), convWidth % (KnobScale.h:654), convFade % (KnobScale.h:691), convPitch 0.25x..4x (KnobScale.h:780), spring lines (1..6). convTone no longer exists on the conv face (removed in the face rework, commit 44a78ea). convStartS/convEndS store seconds directly — their per-IR faces come from convTrimScale (KnobScale.h:675), not a toStored split. The dB format() integer-check is std::abs(db - std::trunc(db)) < 0.05 (the original std::abs(db) - std::trunc(db) equals 2|db| for negative db, rendering "-18.0 dB"; fixed and propagated to convGain and reverbDry). T-DAT-001: reverbSharedMod and reverbWave have NO custom scale (sharedMod is plain 0..1; wave is an int 0..4 detent, identity-bound); LoCut uses loCutTaper() (KnobScale.h:816) with toStored(n) = 0.85 * pow(n, 0.7) (0..0.85 fraction for the mode-0 45 Hz HPF blend).
